title: Simultaneous Epp base change for finitely many traits
statement: Let $p$ be prime and let $W_0$ be a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ with perfect residue field $k_0$ and fraction field $K_0$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring, def-weil-field]. Mixed characteristic means characteristic zero for the fraction field and characteristic $p$ for the residue field; perfect means that Frobenius $x\mapsto x^p$ is surjective. Let $I$ be a finite set. For each $i\in I$ let $T_i$ be an excellent discrete valuation ring with an injective local map $W_0\hookrightarrow T_i$ [def-exc-excellent-ring], fraction field $F_i$, and residue field $\kappa_i$. Local means that the inverse image of the maximal ideal is the maximal ideal. Assume that every element of $\bigcap_{n\geq0}\kappa_i^{p^n}$ is algebraic over the induced copy of $k_0$, where $\kappa_i^{p^n}=\{x^{p^n}:x\in\kappa_i\}$. Then there is an injective local map $W_0\hookrightarrow W$ making $W$ a finite $W_0$-module, where $W$ is a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ whose residue field is a finite extension of $k_0$, hence perfect [def-weil-finitely-generated-module, def-pc-field-extension]. Write $K=\operatorname{Frac}(W)$ and let $\pi$ be any uniformizer of $W$. For each $i$, take any field factor $E$ of $F_i\otimes_{K_0}K$; the tensor product is a finite product of fields, and field factor means a quotient by a maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Let $B_{i,E}\subset E$ be the integral closure of the image of $T_i\otimes_{W_0}W$ in $E$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then $B_{i,E}/\pi B_{i,E}$ is reduced: it has no nonzero nilpotent elements. The rings $T_i$ need not be complete, and $I$ may be empty.
